props.name: scrollEnabled
props.description: If false, scrolling of the text view will be disabled. The default value is true. Only works with multiline={true}

props.name: lineBreakStrategyIOS
props.description: Set line break strategy on iOS.

props.name: lineBreakModeIOS
props.description: Set line break mode on iOS.

props.name: smartInsertDelete
props.description:
If `false`, the iOS system will not insert an extra space after a paste operation
neither delete one or two spaces after a cut or delete operation.

The default value is `true`.

props.name: cursorColor
props.description:
When provided it will set the color of the cursor (or "caret") in the component.
Unlike the behavior of `selectionColor` the cursor color will be set independently
from the color of the text selection box.

props.name: selectionHandleColor
props.description:
When provided it will set the color of the selection handles when highlighting text.
Unlike the behavior of `selectionColor` the handle color will be set independently
from the color of the text selection box.

props.name: importantForAutofill
props.description:
Determines whether the individual fields in your app should be included in a
view structure for autofill purposes on Android API Level 26+. Defaults to auto.
To disable auto complete, use `off`.

*Android Only*

The following values work on Android only:

- `auto` - let Android decide
- `no` - not important for autofill
- `noExcludeDescendants` - this view and its children aren't important for autofill
- `yes` - is important for autofill
- `yesExcludeDescendants` - this view is important for autofill but its children aren't

props.name: disableFullscreenUI
props.description:
When false, if there is a small amount of space available around a text input (e.g. landscape orientation on a phone),
  the OS may choose to have the user edit the text inside of a full screen text input mode.
When true, this feature is disabled and users will always edit the text directly inside of the text input.
Defaults to false.

props.name: inlineImageLeft
props.description: If defined, the provided image resource will be rendered on the left.

props.name: inlineImagePadding
props.description: Padding between the inline image, if any, and the text input itself.

props.name: numberOfLines
props.description:
Sets the number of lines for a TextInput.
Use it with multiline set to true to be able to fill the lines.

props.name: returnKeyLabel
props.description: Sets the return key to the label. Use it instead of `returnKeyType`.

props.name: textBreakStrategy
props.description:
Set text break strategy on Android API Level 23+, possible values are simple, highQuality, balanced
The default value is simple.

props.name: underlineColorAndroid
props.description: The color of the textInput underline.

props.name: textAlignVertical
props.description: Vertically align text when `multiline` is set to true

props.name: showSoftInputOnFocus
props.description: When false, it will prevent the soft keyboard from showing when the field is focused. The default value is true

props.name: verticalAlign
props.description: Vertically align text when `multiline` is set to true

props.name: status
props.description: Status of the input field. Can be 'error', 'success', or 'default'.

props.name: label
props.description: String that specifies the text at the top of the text input.

props.name: inverted
props.description: Adapts the component to show the inverted mode related to colors

props.name: disabled
props.description: Option to specify if the TextInput is disabled

props.name: keyboardAccessoryID
props.description: ID for the keyboard accessory view. Only available on iOS.

props.name: keyboardAccessoryText
props.description: Text for the keyboard accessory view. Only available on iOS.

props.name: keyboardAccesoryOnPress
props.description: Function that is called when the keyboard accessory view is pressed.

props.name: helperAlignment
props.description: Alignment of the helper text and icon

props.name: value
props.description:
The value to show for the text input. TextInput is a controlled component,
which means the native value will be forced to match this value prop if provided.
For most uses this works great, but in some cases this may cause flickering - one common cause is preventing edits by keeping value the same.
In addition to simply setting the same value, either set editable={false},
or set/update maxLength to prevent unwanted edits without flicker.

props.name: onChangeText
props.description:
Callback that is called when the text input's text changes.
Changed text is passed as an argument to the callback handler.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input is focused

props.name: onBlur
props.description:
Callback that is called when the text input is blurred

Note: If you are trying to find the last value of TextInput, you can use the `onEndEditing`
event, which is fired upon completion of editing.

props.name: maxLength
props.description:
Limits the maximum number of characters that can be entered.
Use this instead of implementing the logic in JS to avoid flicker.

props.name: testID
props.description: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests

props.name: allowFontScaling
props.description:
Specifies whether fonts should scale to respect Text Size accessibility settings.
The default is `true`.

props.name: autoCapitalize
props.description:
Can tell TextInput to automatically capitalize certain characters.
     characters: all characters,
     words: first letter of each word
     sentences: first letter of each sentence (default)
     none: don't auto capitalize anything

https://reactnative.dev/docs/textinput#autocapitalize

props.name: autoComplete
props.description:
Specifies autocomplete hints for the system, so it can provide autofill.
On Android, the system will always attempt to offer autofill by using heuristics to identify the type of content.
To disable autocomplete, set autoComplete to off.

The following values work across platforms:

- `additional-name`
- `address-line1`
- `address-line2`
- `cc-number`
- `country`
- `current-password`
- `email`
- `family-name`
- `given-name`
- `honorific-prefix`
- `honorific-suffix`
- `name`
- `new-password`

- `one-time-code`
- `postal-code`
- `street-address`
- `tel`
- `username`

The following values work on iOS only:

- `nickname`
- `organization`
- `organization-title`
- `url`

The following values work on Android only:

- `birthdate-day`
- `birthdate-full`
- `birthdate-month`
- `birthdate-year`
- `cc-csc`
- `cc-exp`
- `cc-exp-day`
- `cc-exp-month`
- `cc-exp-year`
- `gender`
- `name-family`
- `name-given`
- `name-middle`
- `name-middle-initial`
- `name-prefix`
- `name-suffix`
- `password`
- `password-new`
- `postal-address`
- `postal-address-country`
- `postal-address-extended`
- `postal-address-extended-postal-code`
- `postal-address-locality`
- `postal-address-region`
- `sms-otp`
- `tel-country-code`
- `tel-national`
- `tel-device`
- `username-new`

props.name: autoCorrect
props.description:
If false, disables auto-correct.
The default value is true.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description:
If true, focuses the input on componentDidMount.
The default value is false.

props.name: blurOnSubmit
props.description:
If `true`, the text field will blur when submitted.
The default value is true for single-line fields and false for
multiline fields. Note that for multiline fields, setting `blurOnSubmit`
to `true` means that pressing return will blur the field and trigger the
`onSubmitEditing` event instead of inserting a newline into the field.

props.name: submitBehavior
props.description:
When the return key is pressed,

For single line inputs:

- `'newline`' defaults to `'blurAndSubmit'`
- `undefined` defaults to `'blurAndSubmit'`

For multiline inputs:

- `'newline'` adds a newline
- `undefined` defaults to `'newline'`

For both single line and multiline inputs:

- `'submit'` will only send a submit event and not blur the input
- `'blurAndSubmit`' will both blur the input and send a submit event

props.name: caretHidden
props.description: If true, caret is hidden. The default value is false.

props.name: contextMenuHidden
props.description: If true, context menu is hidden. The default value is false.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description:
Provides an initial value that will change when the user starts typing.
Useful for simple use-cases where you don't want to deal with listening to events
and updating the value prop to keep the controlled state in sync.

props.name: editable
props.description: If false, text is not editable. The default value is true.

props.name: keyboardType
props.description:
enum("default", 'numeric', 'email-address', "ascii-capable", 'numbers-and-punctuation', 'url', 'number-pad', 'phone-pad', 'name-phone-pad',
'decimal-pad', 'twitter', 'web-search', 'visible-password')
Determines which keyboard to open, e.g.numeric.
The following values work across platforms: - default - numeric - email-address - phone-pad
The following values work on iOS: - ascii-capable - numbers-and-punctuation - url - number-pad - name-phone-pad - decimal-pad - twitter - web-search
The following values work on Android: - visible-password

props.name: inputMode
props.description: Works like the inputmode attribute in HTML, it determines which keyboard to open, e.g. numeric and has precedence over keyboardType.

props.name: multiline
props.description: If true, the text input can be multiple lines. The default value is false.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input's text changes.

props.name: onContentSizeChange
props.description:
Callback that is called when the text input's content size changes.
This will be called with
`{ nativeEvent: { contentSize: { width, height } } }`.

Only called for multiline text inputs.

props.name: onEndEditing
props.description: Callback that is called when text input ends.

props.name: onPress
props.description: Called when a single tap gesture is detected.

props.name: onPressIn
props.description: Callback that is called when a touch is engaged.

props.name: onPressOut
props.description: Callback that is called when a touch is released.

props.name: onSelectionChange
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input selection is changed.

props.name: onSubmitEditing
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input's submit button is pressed.

props.name: onScroll
props.description:
Invoked on content scroll with
 `{ nativeEvent: { contentOffset: { x, y } } }`.

May also contain other properties from ScrollEvent but on Android contentSize is not provided for performance reasons.

props.name: onKeyPress
props.description:
Callback that is called when a key is pressed.
This will be called with
 `{ nativeEvent: { key: keyValue } }`
where keyValue is 'Enter' or 'Backspace' for respective keys and the typed-in character otherwise including ' ' for space.

Fires before onChange callbacks.
Note: on Android only the inputs from soft keyboard are handled, not the hardware keyboard inputs.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The string that will be rendered before text input has been entered

props.name: placeholderTextColor
props.description: The text color of the placeholder string

props.name: readOnly
props.description: If `true`, text is not editable. The default value is `false`.

props.name: returnKeyType
props.description:
enum('default', 'go', 'google', 'join', 'next', 'route', 'search', 'send', 'yahoo', 'done', 'emergency-call')
Determines how the return key should look.

props.name: enterKeyHint
props.description:
Determines what text should be shown to the return key on virtual keyboards.
Has precedence over the returnKeyType prop.

props.name: secureTextEntry
props.description:
If true, the text input obscures the text entered so that sensitive text like passwords stay secure.
The default value is false.

props.name: selectTextOnFocus
props.description: If true, all text will automatically be selected on focus

props.name: selection
props.type: { start: number; end?: number | undefined; } | undefined
props.description:
The start and end of the text input's selection. Set start and end to
the same value to position the cursor.

props.name: selectionColor
props.description: The highlight (and cursor on ios) color of the text input

props.name: textAlign
props.description: Align the input text to the left, center, or right sides of the input field.

props.name: inputAccessoryViewID
props.description:
Used to connect to an InputAccessoryView. Not part of react-natives documentation, but present in examples and
code.
See https://reactnative.dev/docs/inputaccessoryview for more information.

props.name: inputAccessoryViewButtonLabel
props.description: An optional label that overrides the default input accessory view button label.

props.name: maxFontSizeMultiplier
props.description:
Specifies largest possible scale a font can reach when allowFontScaling is enabled. Possible values:
- null/undefined (default): inherit from the parent node or the global default (0)
- 0: no max, ignore parent/global default
- >= 1: sets the maxFontSizeMultiplier of this node to this value

props.name: children
props.description: React children.

props.name: hitSlop
props.description:
This defines how far a touch event can start away from the view.
Typical interface guidelines recommend touch targets that are at least
30 - 40 points/density-independent pixels. If a Touchable view has
a height of 20 the touchable height can be extended to 40 with
hitSlop={{top: 10, bottom: 10, left: 0, right: 0}}
NOTE The touch area never extends past the parent view bounds and
the Z-index of sibling views always takes precedence if a touch
hits two overlapping views.

props.name: id
props.description: Used to reference react managed views from native code.

props.name: needsOffscreenAlphaCompositing
props.description:
Whether this view needs to rendered offscreen and composited with an alpha in order to preserve 100% correct colors and blending behavior.
The default (false) falls back to drawing the component and its children
with an alpha applied to the paint used to draw each element instead of rendering the full component offscreen and compositing it back with an alpha value.
This default may be noticeable and undesired in the case where the View you are setting an opacity on
has multiple overlapping elements (e.g. multiple overlapping Views, or text and a background).

Rendering offscreen to preserve correct alpha behavior is extremely expensive
and hard to debug for non-native developers, which is why it is not turned on by default.
If you do need to enable this property for an animation,
consider combining it with renderToHardwareTextureAndroid if the view contents are static (i.e. it doesn't need to be redrawn each frame).
If that property is enabled, this View will be rendered off-screen once,
saved in a hardware texture, and then composited onto the screen with an alpha each frame without having to switch rendering targets on the GPU.

props.name: onLayout
props.description:
Invoked on mount and layout changes with

{nativeEvent: { layout: {x, y, width, height}}}.

props.name: pointerEvents
removeClippedSubviews
props.description:
This is a special performance property exposed by RCTView and is useful for scrolling content when there are many subviews,
most of which are offscreen. For this property to be effective, it must be applied to a view that contains many subviews that extend outside its bound.
The subviews must also have overflow: hidden, as should the containing view (or one of its superviews).

props.name: nativeID
props.description: Used to reference react managed views from native code.

props.name: collapsable
props.description:
Views that are only used to layout their children or otherwise don't draw anything
may be automatically removed from the native hierarchy as an optimization.
Set this property to false to disable this optimization and ensure that this View exists in the native view hierarchy.

props.name: collapsableChildren
props.description:
Setting to false prevents direct children of the view from being removed
from the native view hierarchy, similar to the effect of setting
`collapsable={false}` on each child.

props.name: renderToHardwareTextureAndroid
props.description:
Whether this view should render itself (and all of its children) into a single hardware texture on the GPU.

On Android, this is useful for animations and interactions that only modify opacity, rotation, translation, and/or scale:
in those cases, the view doesn't have to be redrawn and display lists don't need to be re-executed. The texture can just be
re-used and re-composited with different parameters. The downside is that this can use up limited video memory, so this prop should be set back to false at the end of the interaction/animation.

props.name: focusable
props.description: Whether this `View` should be focusable with a non-touch input device, eg. receive focus with a hardware keyboard.

props.name: tabIndex
props.description:
Indicates whether this `View` should be focusable with a non-touch input device, eg. receive focus with a hardware keyboard.
See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/tabindex
for more details.

Supports the following values:
-  0 (View is focusable)
- -1 (View is not focusable)

props.name: shouldRasterizeIOS
props.description:
Whether this view should be rendered as a bitmap before compositing.

On iOS, this is useful for animations and interactions that do not modify this component's dimensions nor its children;
for example, when translating the position of a static view, rasterization allows the renderer to reuse a cached bitmap of a static view
and quickly composite it during each frame.

Rasterization incurs an off-screen drawing pass and the bitmap consumes memory.
Test and measure when using this property.

props.name: isTVSelectable
props.description:
*(Apple TV only)* When set to true, this view will be focusable
and navigable using the Apple TV remote.

props.name: hasTVPreferredFocus
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be set to true to force the Apple TV focus engine to move focus to this view.

props.name: tvParallaxShiftDistanceX
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus.  Defaults to 2.0.

props.name: tvParallaxShiftDistanceY
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus.  Defaults to 2.0.

props.name: tvParallaxTiltAngle
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus.  Defaults to 0.05.

props.name: tvParallaxMagnification
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus.  Defaults to 1.0.

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponder
props.description: Does this view want to become responder on the start of a touch?

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponder
props.description: Called for every touch move on the View when it is not the responder: does this view want to "claim" touch responsiveness?

props.name: onResponderEnd
props.description: If the View returns true and attempts to become the responder, one of the following will happen:

props.name: onResponderGrant
props.description:
The View is now responding for touch events.
This is the time to highlight and show the user what is happening

props.name: onResponderReject
props.description: Something else is the responder right now and will not release it

props.name: onResponderMove
props.description: The user is moving their finger

props.name: onResponderRelease
props.description: Fired at the end of the touch, ie "touchUp"

props.name: onResponderTerminationRequest
props.description:
Something else wants to become responder.
Should this view release the responder? Returning true allows release

props.name: onResponderTerminate
props.description:
The responder has been taken from the View.
Might be taken by other views after a call to onResponderTerminationRequest,
or might be taken by the OS without asking (happens with control center/ notification center on iOS)

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:
onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern,
where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.
This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable.

However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder.
This can be handled by using the capture phase.
Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component,
it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture.
So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:
onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern,
where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.
This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable.

However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder.
This can be handled by using the capture phase.
Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component,
it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture.
So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: accessible
props.description:
When true, indicates that the view is an accessibility element.
By default, all the touchable elements are accessible.

props.name: accessibilityActions
props.type: readonly Readonly<{ name: AccessibilityActionName | string; label?: string | undefined; }>[] | undefined
props.description: Provides an array of custom actions available for accessibility.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description:
Overrides the text that's read by the screen reader when the user interacts with the element. By default, the
label is constructed by traversing all the children and accumulating all the Text nodes separated by space.

props.name: aria-label
props.description:
Alias for accessibilityLabel  https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#accessibilitylabel
https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/34424

props.name: accessibilityRole
props.description: Accessibility Role tells a person using either VoiceOver on iOS or TalkBack on Android the type of element that is focused on.

props.name: accessibilityState
props.description: Accessibility State tells a person using either VoiceOver on iOS or TalkBack on Android the state of the element currently focused on.

props.name: aria-busy
props.description:
alias for accessibilityState

see https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitystate

props.name: accessibilityHint
props.description: An accessibility hint helps users understand what will happen when they perform an action on the accessibility element when that result is not obvious from the accessibility label.

props.name: accessibilityValue
props.description:
Represents the current value of a component. It can be a textual description of a component's value, or for range-based components, such as sliders and progress bars,
it contains range information (minimum, current, and maximum).

props.name: onAccessibilityAction
props.description: When `accessible` is true, the system will try to invoke this function when the user performs an accessibility custom action.

props.name: importantForAccessibility
props.description: [Android] Controlling if a view fires accessibility events and if it is reported to accessibility services.

props.name: aria-hidden
props.description:
A value indicating whether the accessibility elements contained within
this accessibility element are hidden.

props.name: role
props.description: Indicates to accessibility services to treat UI component like a specific role.

props.name: accessibilityLabelledBy
props.description:
Identifies the element that labels the element it is applied to. When the assistive technology focuses on the component with this props,
the text is read aloud. The value should should match the nativeID of the related element.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description:
Identifies the element that labels the element it is applied to. When the assistive technology focuses on the component with this props,
the text is read aloud. The value should should match the nativeID of the related element.

props.name: accessibilityLiveRegion
props.description:
Indicates to accessibility services whether the user should be notified
when this view changes. Works for Android API >= 19 only.

props.name: aria-live
props.description:
Indicates to accessibility services whether the user should be notified
when this view changes. Works for Android API >= 19 only.

props.name: screenReaderFocusable
props.description: Enables the view to be screen reader focusable, not keyboard focusable.

props.name: accessibilityElementsHidden
props.description:
A Boolean value indicating whether the accessibility elements contained within this accessibility element
are hidden to the screen reader.

props.name: accessibilityViewIsModal
props.description: A Boolean value indicating whether VoiceOver should ignore the elements within views that are siblings of the receiver.

props.name: onAccessibilityEscape
props.description: When accessible is true, the system will invoke this function when the user performs the escape gesture (scrub with two fingers).

props.name: onAccessibilityTap
props.description: When `accessible` is true, the system will try to invoke this function when the user performs accessibility tap gesture.

props.name: onMagicTap
props.description: When accessible is true, the system will invoke this function when the user performs the magic tap gesture.

props.name: accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors
props.description: https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilityignoresinvertcolorsios

props.name: accessibilityLanguage
props.description:
By using the accessibilityLanguage property, the screen reader will understand which language to use while reading the element's label, value and hint. The provided string value must follow the BCP 47 specification (https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp47).
https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitylanguage-ios

props.name: accessibilityShowsLargeContentViewer
props.description:
A Boolean value that indicates whether or not to show the item in the large content viewer.
Available on iOS 13.0+
https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilityshowslargecontentviewer

props.name: accessibilityLargeContentTitle
props.description:
When `accessibilityShowsLargeContentViewer` is set, this string will be used as title for the large content viewer.
https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitylargecontenttitle

props.name: accessibilityRespondsToUserInteraction
props.description:
Blocks the user from interacting with the component through keyboard while still allowing
screen reader to interact with it if this View is still accessible.

props.name: disableKeyboardShortcuts

props.name: disableFullscreenUI

props.name: numberOfLines

props.name: value
props.description:

which means the native value will be forced to match this value prop if provided.
For most uses this works great, but in some cases this may cause flickering - one common cause is preventing edits by keeping value the same.
In addition to simply setting the same value, either set editable={false},

props.name: onChangeText

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input is focused

props.name: onBlur
props.description:
Callback that is called when the text input is blurred

Note: If you are trying to find the last value of TextInput, you can use the `onEndEditing`

props.name: maxLength
props.description:

Use this instead of implementing the logic in JS to avoid flicker.

props.name: testID
props.description: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests

props.name: allowFontScaling
props.description:
Specifies whether fonts should scale to respect Text Size accessibility settings.
The default is `true`.

props.name: autoCapitalize

Can tell TextInput to automatically capitalize certain characters.

props.name: autoCorrect
props.description:
If false, disables auto-correct.
The default value is true.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description:
If true, focuses the input on componentDidMount.
The default value is false.

props.name: blurOnSubmit
props.description:
If `true`, the text field will blur when submitted.
The default value is true for single-line fields and false for
multiline fields. Note that for multiline fields, setting `blurOnSubmit`
to `true` means that pressing return will blur the field and trigger the
`onSubmitEditing` event instead of inserting a newline into the field.

props.name: submitBehavior
props.description:
When the return key is pressed,

For single line inputs:

- `'newline`' defaults to `'blurAndSubmit'`
- `undefined` defaults to `'blurAndSubmit'`

For multiline inputs:

- `'newline'` adds a newline
- `undefined` defaults to `'newline'`

For both single line and multiline inputs:

- `'submit'` will only send a submit event and not blur the input
- `'blurAndSubmit`' will both blur the input and send a submit event

props.name: caretHidden
props.description: If true, caret is hidden. The default value is false.

props.name: contextMenuHidden
props.description: If true, context menu is hidden. The default value is false.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description:
Provides an initial value that will change when the user starts typing.
Useful for simple use-cases where you don't want to deal with listening to events
and updating the value prop to keep the controlled state in sync.

props.name: editable
props.description: If false, text is not editable. The default value is true.

props.name: keyboardType
props.description:
enum("default", 'numeric', 'email-address', "ascii-capable", 'numbers-and-punctuation', 'url', 'number-pad', 'phone-pad', 'name-phone-pad',
'decimal-pad', 'twitter', 'web-search', 'visible-password')

The following values work across platforms: - default - numeric - email-address - phone-pad
The following values work on iOS: - ascii-capable - numbers-and-punctuation - url - number-pad - name-phone-pad - decimal-pad - twitter - web-search
The following values work on Android: - visible-password

props.name: inputMode
props.description: Works like the inputmode attribute in HTML, it determines which keyboard to open, e.g. numeric and has precedence over keyboardType.

props.name: multiline
props.description: If true, the text input can be multiple lines. The default value is false.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input's text changes.

props.name: onContentSizeChange
props.description:
Callback that is called when the text input's content size changes.
This will be called with
`{ nativeEvent: { contentSize: { width, height } } }`.

Only called for multiline text inputs.

props.name: onEndEditing
props.description: Callback that is called when text input ends.

props.name: onPress
props.description: Called when a single tap gesture is detected.

props.name: onPressIn
props.description: Callback that is called when a touch is engaged.

props.name: onPressOut
props.description: Callback that is called when a touch is released.

props.name: onSelectionChange

props.name: onSubmitEditing

props.name: onScroll
props.description:
Invoked on content scroll with

May also contain other properties from ScrollEvent but on Android contentSize is not provided for performance reasons.

props.name: onKeyPress
props.description:
Callback that is called when a key is pressed.
This will be called with
 `{ nativeEvent: { key: keyValue } }`
where keyValue is 'Enter' or 'Backspace' for respective keys and the typed-in character otherwise including ' ' for space.

Fires before onChange callbacks.
Note: on Android only the inputs from soft keyboard are handled, not the hardware keyboard inputs.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The string that will be rendered before text input has been entered

props.name: placeholderTextColor
props.description: The text color of the placeholder string

props.name: readOnly
props.description: If `true`, text is not editable. The default value is `false`.

props.name: returnKeyType
props.description:
enum('default', 'go', 'google', 'join', 'next', 'route', 'search', 'send', 'yahoo', 'done', 'emergency-call')
Determines how the return key should look.

props.name: enterKeyHint
props.description:
Determines what text should be shown to the return key on virtual keyboards.
Has precedence over the returnKeyType prop.

props.name: secureTextEntry
props.description:
If true, the text input obscures the text entered so that sensitive text like passwords stay secure.
The default value is false.

props.name: selectTextOnFocus
props.description: If true, all text will automatically be selected on focus

props.name: selection
props.type: { start: number; end?: number | undefined; } | undefined
props.description:
The start and end of the text input's selection. Set start and end to
the same value to position the cursor.

props.name: selectionColor
props.description: The highlight (and cursor on ios) color of the text input

props.name: textAlign
props.description: Align the input text to the left, center, or right sides of the input field.

props.name: inputAccessoryViewID
props.description:
Used to connect to an InputAccessoryView. Not part of react-natives documentation, but present in examples and
code.
See https://reactnative.dev/docs/inputaccessoryview for more information.

props.name: inputAccessoryViewButtonLabel
props.description: An optional label that overrides the default input accessory view button label.

props.name: maxFontSizeMultiplier
props.description:
Specifies largest possible scale a font can reach when allowFontScaling is enabled. Possible values:
- null/undefined (default): inherit from the parent node or the global default (0)
- 0: no max, ignore parent/global default
- >= 1: sets the maxFontSizeMultiplier of this node to this value

props.name: hitSlop
props.description:
This defines how far a touch event can start away from the view.
Typical interface guidelines recommend touch targets that are at least
30 - 40 points/density-independent pixels. If a Touchable view has
a height of 20 the touchable height can be extended to 40 with
hitSlop={{top: 10, bottom: 10, left: 0, right: 0}}
NOTE The touch area never extends past the parent view bounds and
the Z-index of sibling views always takes precedence if a touch
hits two overlapping views.

props.name: id
props.description: Used to reference react managed views from native code.

props.name: needsOffscreenAlphaCompositing
props.description:
Whether this view needs to rendered offscreen and composited with an alpha in order to preserve 100% correct colors and blending behavior.
The default (false) falls back to drawing the component and its children
with an alpha applied to the paint used to draw each element instead of rendering the full component offscreen and compositing it back with an alpha value.
This default may be noticeable and undesired in the case where the View you are setting an opacity on
has multiple overlapping elements (e.g. multiple overlapping Views, or text and a background).

Rendering offscreen to preserve correct alpha behavior is extremely expensive
and hard to debug for non-native developers, which is why it is not turned on by default.
If you do need to enable this property for an animation,
consider combining it with renderToHardwareTextureAndroid if the view contents are static (i.e. it doesn't need to be redrawn each frame).
If that property is enabled, this View will be rendered off-screen once,
saved in a hardware texture, and then composited onto the screen with an alpha each frame without having to switch rendering targets on the GPU.

props.name: onLayout
props.description:
Invoked on mount and layout changes with

{nativeEvent: { layout: {x, y, width, height}}}.

props.name: pointerEvents
removeClippedSubviews
props.description:
This is a special performance property exposed by RCTView and is useful for scrolling content when there are many subviews,
most of which are offscreen. For this property to be effective, it must be applied to a view that contains many subviews that extend outside its bound.
The subviews must also have overflow: hidden, as should the containing view (or one of its superviews).

props.name: nativeID
props.description: Used to reference react managed views from native code.

props.name: collapsable
props.description:
Views that are only used to layout their children or otherwise don't draw anything
may be automatically removed from the native hierarchy as an optimization.
Set this property to false to disable this optimization and ensure that this View exists in the native view hierarchy.

props.name: collapsableChildren
props.description:
Setting to false prevents direct children of the view from being removed
from the native view hierarchy, similar to the effect of setting
`collapsable={false}` on each child.

props.name: renderToHardwareTextureAndroid
props.description:
Whether this view should render itself (and all of its children) into a single hardware texture on the GPU.

On Android, this is useful for animations and interactions that only modify opacity, rotation, translation, and/or scale:
in those cases, the view doesn't have to be redrawn and display lists don't need to be re-executed. The texture can just be
re-used and re-composited with different parameters. The downside is that this can use up limited video memory, so this prop should be set back to false at the end of the interaction/animation.

props.name: focusable
props.description: Whether this `View` should be focusable with a non-touch input device, eg. receive focus with a hardware keyboard.

props.name: tabIndex
props.description:
Indicates whether this `View` should be focusable with a non-touch input device, eg. receive focus with a hardware keyboard.
See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/tabindex
for more details.

Supports the following values:
-  0 (View is focusable)
- -1 (View is not focusable)

props.name: shouldRasterizeIOS
props.description:
Whether this view should be rendered as a bitmap before compositing.

On iOS, this is useful for animations and interactions that do not modify this component's dimensions nor its children;
for example, when translating the position of a static view, rasterization allows the renderer to reuse a cached bitmap of a static view
and quickly composite it during each frame.

Rasterization incurs an off-screen drawing pass and the bitmap consumes memory.
Test and measure when using this property.

props.name: isTVSelectable
props.description:
*(Apple TV only)* When set to true, this view will be focusable
and navigable using the Apple TV remote.

props.name: hasTVPreferredFocus
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be set to true to force the Apple TV focus engine to move focus to this view.

props.name: tvParallaxShiftDistanceX
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus.  Defaults to 2.0.

props.name: tvParallaxShiftDistanceY
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus.  Defaults to 2.0.

props.name: tvParallaxTiltAngle
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus.  Defaults to 0.05.

props.name: tvParallaxMagnification
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus.  Defaults to 1.0.

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponder
props.description: Does this view want to become responder on the start of a touch?

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponder
props.description: Called for every touch move on the View when it is not the responder: does this view want to "claim" touch responsiveness?

props.name: onResponderEnd
props.description: If the View returns true and attempts to become the responder, one of the following will happen:

props.name: onResponderGrant
props.description:
The View is now responding for touch events.
This is the time to highlight and show the user what is happening

props.name: onResponderReject
props.description: Something else is the responder right now and will not release it

props.name: onResponderMove
props.description: The user is moving their finger

props.name: onResponderRelease
props.description: Fired at the end of the touch, ie "touchUp"

props.name: onResponderTerminationRequest
props.description:
Something else wants to become responder.
Should this view release the responder? Returning true allows release

props.name: onResponderTerminate
props.description:
The responder has been taken from the View.
Might be taken by other views after a call to onResponderTerminationRequest,
or might be taken by the OS without asking (happens with control center/ notification center on iOS)

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:
onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern,
where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.
This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable.

However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder.
This can be handled by using the capture phase.
Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component,
it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture.
So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:
onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern,
where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.
This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable.

However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder.
This can be handled by using the capture phase.
Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component,
it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture.
So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: accessible

When true, indicates that the view is an accessibility element.
By default, all the touchable elements are accessible.

props.name: accessibilityLabel

Overrides the text that's read by the screen reader when the user interacts with the element. By default, the
label is constructed by traversing all the children and accumulating all the Text nodes separated by space.

props.name: aria-label
props.description:
Alias for accessibilityLabel  https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#accessibilitylabel
https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/34424

props.name: accessibilityRole
props.description: Accessibility Role tells a person using either VoiceOver on iOS or TalkBack on Android the type of element that is focused on.

props.name: accessibilityState
props.description: Accessibility State tells a person using either VoiceOver on iOS or TalkBack on Android the state of the element currently focused on.

props.name: aria-busy
props.description:
alias for accessibilityState

see https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitystate

props.name: accessibilityHint
props.description: An accessibility hint helps users understand what will happen when they perform an action on the accessibility element when that result is not obvious from the accessibility label.

props.name: accessibilityValue
props.description:
Represents the current value of a component. It can be a textual description of a component's value, or for range-based components, such as sliders and progress bars,
it contains range information (minimum, current, and maximum).

props.name: onAccessibilityAction
props.description: When `accessible` is true, the system will try to invoke this function when the user performs an accessibility custom action.

props.name: importantForAccessibility
props.description: [Android] Controlling if a view fires accessibility events and if it is reported to accessibility services.

props.name: aria-hidden
props.description:

this accessibility element are hidden.

props.name: role
props.description: Indicates to accessibility services to treat UI component like a specific role.

props.name: accessibilityLabelledBy

Identifies the element that labels the element it is applied to. When the assistive technology focuses on the component with this props,
the text is read aloud. The value should should match the nativeID of the related element.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description:
Identifies the element that labels the element it is applied to. When the assistive technology focuses on the component with this props,
the text is read aloud. The value should should match the nativeID of the related element.

props.name: accessibilityLiveRegion
props.description:
Indicates to accessibility services whether the user should be notified
when this view changes. Works for Android API >= 19 only.

props.name: aria-live
props.description:
Indicates to accessibility services whether the user should be notified
when this view changes. Works for Android API >= 19 only.

props.name: screenReaderFocusable
props.description: Enables the view to be screen reader focusable, not keyboard focusable.

props.name: accessibilityElementsHidden
props.description:
A Boolean value indicating whether the accessibility elements contained within this accessibility element

it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.description: If the View returns true and attempts to become the responder, one of the following will happen:

props.name: onResponderReject
props.description: Something else is the responder right now and will not release it

props.name: onResponderMove
props.description: The user is moving their finger

props.name: onResponderRelease
props.description: Fired at the end of the touch, ie "touchUp"

props.name: onResponderTerminationRequest
props.description:
Something else wants to become responder.
Should this view release the responder? Returning true allows release

props.name: onResponderTerminate
props.description:
The responder has been taken from the View.
Might be taken by other views after a call to onResponderTerminationRequest,
or might be taken by the OS without asking (happens with control center/ notification center on iOS)

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:
onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern,
where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.
This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable.

However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder.
This can be handled by using the capture phase.
Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component,
it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture.
So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:

props.name: needsOffscreenAlphaCompositing
props.description:
Whether this view needs to rendered offscreen and composited with an alpha in order to preserve 100% correct colors and blending behavior.
The default (false) falls back to drawing the component and its children
with an alpha applied to the paint used to draw each element instead of rendering the full component offscreen and compositing it back with an alpha value.
This default may be noticeable and undesired in the case where the View you are setting an opacity on
has multiple overlapping elements (e.g. multiple overlapping Views, or text and a background).

Rendering offscreen to preserve correct alpha behavior is extremely expensive
and hard to debug for non-native developers, which is why it is not turned on by default.
If you do need to enable this property for an animation,
consider combining it with renderToHardwareTextureAndroid if the view contents are static (i.e. it doesn't need to be redrawn each frame).
If that property is enabled, this View will be rendered off-screen once,
saved in a hardware texture, and then composited onto the screen with an alpha each frame without having to switch rendering targets on the GPU.

props.name: removeClippedSubviews
props.description:
This is a special performance property exposed by RCTView and is useful for scrolling content when there are many subviews,
most of which are offscreen. For this property to be effective, it must be applied to a view that contains many subviews that extend outside its bound.
The subviews must also have overflow: hidden, as should the containing view (or one of its superviews).

Set this property to false to disable this optimization and ensure that this View exists in the native view hierarchy.

props.name: collapsableChildren
props.description:

props.name: renderToHardwareTextureAndroid
props.description:
Whether this view should render itself (and all of its children) into a single hardware texture on the GPU.

On Android, this is useful for animations and interactions that only modify opacity, rotation, translation, and/or scale:
in those cases, the view doesn't have to be redrawn and display lists don't need to be re-executed. The texture can just be
re-used and re-composited with different parameters. The downside is that this can use up limited video memory, so this prop should be set back to false at the end of the interaction/animation.

props.name: tabIndex

- -1 (View is not focusable)

On iOS, this is useful for animations and interactions that do not modify this component's dimensions nor its children;
for example, when translating the position of a static view, rasterization allows the renderer to reuse a cached bitmap of a static view
and quickly composite it during each frame.

Rasterization incurs an off-screen drawing pass and the bitmap consumes memory.
Test and measure when using this property.

This can be one of the following values:

- `head` - The line is displayed so that the end fits in the container and the missing text
at the beginning of the line is indicated by an ellipsis glyph. e.g., "...wxyz"
- `middle` - The line is displayed so that the beginning and end fit in the container and the
missing text in the middle is indicated by an ellipsis glyph. "ab...yz"
- `tail` - The line is displayed so that the beginning fits in the container and the
missing text at the end of the line is indicated by an ellipsis glyph. e.g., "abcd..."
- `clip` - Lines are not drawn past the edge of the text container.

The default is `tail`.

`numberOfLines` must be set in conjunction with this prop.

> `clip` is working only for iOS

Overrides the text that's read by the screen reader when the user interacts with the element. By default, the
label is constructed by traversing all the children and accumulating all the Text nodes separated by space.

props.name: aria-label
props.description:
Alias for accessibilityLabel  https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#accessibilitylabel
https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/34424

props.name: accessibilityRole
props.description: Accessibility Role tells a person using either VoiceOver on iOS or TalkBack on Android the type of element that is focused on.

props.name: accessibilityState
props.description: Accessibility State tells a person using either VoiceOver on iOS or TalkBack on Android the state of the element currently focused on.

props.name: aria-busy
props.description:
alias for accessibilityState

see https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitystate

props.name: accessibilityHint
props.description: An accessibility hint helps users understand what will happen when they perform an action on the accessibility element when that result is not obvious from the accessibility label.

props.name: accessibilityValue
props.description:
Represents the current value of a component. It can be a textual description of a component's value, or for range-based components, such as sliders and progress bars,
it contains range information (minimum, current, and maximum).

props.name: onAccessibilityAction
props.description: When `accessible` is true, the system will try to invoke this function when the user performs an accessibility custom action.

props.name: importantForAccessibility
props.description: [Android] Controlling if a view fires accessibility events and if it is reported to accessibility services.

props.name: aria-hidden
props.description:
A value indicating whether the accessibility elements contained within
this accessibility element are hidden.

props.name: role
props.description: Indicates to accessibility services to treat UI component like a specific role.

props.name: accessibilityLabelledBy
props.description:
Identifies the element that labels the element it is applied to. When the assistive technology focuses on the component with this props,
the text is read aloud. The value should should match the nativeID of the related element.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description:
Identifies the element that labels the element it is applied to. When the assistive technology focuses on the component with this props,
the text is read aloud. The value should should match the nativeID of the related element.

props.name: accessibilityLiveRegion
props.description:
Indicates to accessibility services whether the user should be notified
when this view changes. Works for Android API >= 19 only.

props.name: aria-live
props.description:
Indicates to accessibility services whether the user should be notified
when this view changes. Works for Android API >= 19 only.

props.name: screenReaderFocusable
props.description: Enables the view to be screen reader focusable, not keyboard focusable.

props.name: accessibilityElementsHidden
props.description:
A Boolean value indicating whether the accessibility elements contained within this accessibility element
are hidden to the screen reader.

props.name: accessibilityViewIsModal
props.description: A Boolean value indicating whether VoiceOver should ignore the elements within views that are siblings of the receiver.

props.name: onAccessibilityEscape
props.description: When accessible is true, the system will invoke this function when the user performs the escape gesture (scrub with two fingers).

props.name: onAccessibilityTap
props.description: When `accessible` is true, the system will try to invoke this function when the user performs accessibility tap gesture.

props.name: onMagicTap
props.description: When accessible is true, the system will invoke this function when the user performs the magic tap gesture.

props.name: accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors

props.name: accessibilityLanguage
props.description:

props.name: accessibilityShowsLargeContentViewer
props.description:
A Boolean value that indicates whether or not to show the item in the large content viewer.
Available on iOS 13.0+

props.name: accessibilityLargeContentTitle
props.description:

https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitylargecontenttitle

props.name: accessibilityRespondsToUserInteraction
props.description:
Blocks the user from interacting with the component through keyboard while still allowing
screen reader to interact with it if this View is still accessible.

props.name: variant

props.name: inverted

props.name: value
props.description:
The value to show for the text input. TextInput is a controlled component,
which means the native value will be forced to match this value prop if provided.
For most uses this works great, but in some cases this may cause flickering - one common cause is preventing edits by keeping value the same.
In addition to simply setting the same value, either set editable={false},
or set/update maxLength to prevent unwanted edits without flicker.
Specifies the value of the text input.

props.name: label
props.description: String that specifies the text at the top of the text input.

props.description: Callback that is called when the text input is focused

props.name: onBlur
props.description:
Callback that is called when the text input is blurred

Note: If you are trying to find the last value of TextInput, you can use the `onEndEditing`
event, which is fired upon completion of editing.

props.name: maxLength
props.description:
Limits the maximum number of characters that can be entered.
Use this instead of implementing the logic in JS to avoid flicker.
Specifies the maximum length of the entered text.

props.name: helperMessage
props.description:
This prop is used to additional information to the user,

props.name: disabled

props.name: status

props.name: helperAlignment

props.name: variant
props.description:
Specifies the variant of the text input (text, password, date, textarea).
Specifies the variant of the text input (card-number, text, password, date, textarea).

props.name: allowFontScaling
props.description:
Specifies whether fonts should scale to respect Text Size accessibility settings.
The default is `true`.

props.name: autoCapitalize
props.description:
Can tell TextInput to automatically capitalize certain characters.
     characters: all characters,
     words: first letter of each word
     sentences: first letter of each sentence (default)
     none: don't auto capitalize anything

https://reactnative.dev/docs/textinput#autocapitalize

props.name: autoComplete

Specifies autocomplete hints for the system, so it can provide autofill.
On Android, the system will always attempt to offer autofill by using heuristics to identify the type of content.

props.name: autoCorrect
props.description:
If false, disables auto-correct.
The default value is true.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description:
If true, focuses the input on componentDidMount.
The default value is false.

props.name: blurOnSubmit
props.description:
If `true`, the text field will blur when submitted.
The default value is true for single-line fields and false for
multiline fields. Note that for multiline fields, setting `blurOnSubmit`
to `true` means that pressing return will blur the field and trigger the
`onSubmitEditing` event instead of inserting a newline into the field.

props.name: submitBehavior
props.description:
When the return key is pressed,

For single line inputs:

- `'newline`' defaults to `'blurAndSubmit'`
- `undefined` defaults to `'blurAndSubmit'`

For multiline inputs:

- `'newline'` adds a newline
- `undefined` defaults to `'newline'`

For both single line and multiline inputs:

- `'submit'` will only send a submit event and not blur the input
- `'blurAndSubmit`' will both blur the input and send a submit event

props.name: caretHidden
props.description: If true, caret is hidden. The default value is false.

props.name: contextMenuHidden
props.description: If true, context menu is hidden. The default value is false.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description:
Provides an initial value that will change when the user starts typing.
Useful for simple use-cases where you don't want to deal with listening to events
and updating the value prop to keep the controlled state in sync.

props.name: editable
props.description: If false, text is not editable. The default value is true.

props.name: keyboardType
props.description:
enum("default", 'numeric', 'email-address', "ascii-capable", 'numbers-and-punctuation', 'url', 'number-pad', 'phone-pad', 'name-phone-pad',
'decimal-pad', 'twitter', 'web-search', 'visible-password')
Determines which keyboard to open, e.g.numeric.
The following values work across platforms: - default - numeric - email-address - phone-pad
The following values work on iOS: - ascii-capable - numbers-and-punctuation - url - number-pad - name-phone-pad - decimal-pad - twitter - web-search
The following values work on Android: - visible-password

props.name: inputMode
props.description: Works like the inputmode attribute in HTML, it determines which keyboard to open, e.g. numeric and has precedence over keyboardType.

props.name: multiline
props.description: If true, the text input can be multiple lines. The default value is false.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input's text changes.

props.name: onContentSizeChange
props.description:
Callback that is called when the text input's content size changes.
This will be called with
`{ nativeEvent: { contentSize: { width, height } } }`.

Only called for multiline text inputs.

props.name: onEndEditing
props.description: Callback that is called when text input ends.

props.name: onPress
props.description: Called when a single tap gesture is detected.

props.name: onPressIn
props.description: Callback that is called when a touch is engaged.

props.name: onPressOut
props.description: Callback that is called when a touch is released.

props.name: onSelectionChange
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input selection is changed.

props.name: onSubmitEditing
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input's submit button is pressed.

props.name: onScroll
props.description:
Invoked on content scroll with
 `{ nativeEvent: { contentOffset: { x, y } } }`.

May also contain other properties from ScrollEvent but on Android contentSize is not provided for performance reasons.

props.name: onKeyPress
props.description:
Callback that is called when a key is pressed.
This will be called with
 `{ nativeEvent: { key: keyValue } }`
where keyValue is 'Enter' or 'Backspace' for respective keys and the typed-in character otherwise including ' ' for space.

Fires before onChange callbacks.
Note: on Android only the inputs from soft keyboard are handled, not the hardware keyboard inputs.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The string that will be rendered before text input has been entered

props.name: placeholderTextColor
props.description: The text color of the placeholder string

props.name: readOnly
props.description: If `true`, text is not editable. The default value is `false`.

props.name: returnKeyType
props.description:
enum('default', 'go', 'google', 'join', 'next', 'route', 'search', 'send', 'yahoo', 'done', 'emergency-call')
Determines how the return key should look.

props.name: enterKeyHint
props.description:
Determines what text should be shown to the return key on virtual keyboards.
Has precedence over the returnKeyType prop.

props.name: secureTextEntry
props.description:
If true, the text input obscures the text entered so that sensitive text like passwords stay secure.
The default value is false.

props.name: selectTextOnFocus
props.description: If true, all text will automatically be selected on focus

props.name: selection
props.type: { start: number; end?: number | undefined; } | undefined
props.description:
The start and end of the text input's selection. Set start and end to
the same value to position the cursor.

props.name: selectionColor
props.description: The highlight (and cursor on ios) color of the text input

props.name: textAlign
props.description: Align the input text to the left, center, or right sides of the input field.

props.name: inputAccessoryViewID
props.description:
Used to connect to an InputAccessoryView. Not part of react-natives documentation, but present in examples and
code.
See https://reactnative.dev/docs/inputaccessoryview for more information.

props.name: inputAccessoryViewButtonLabel
props.description: An optional label that overrides the default input accessory view button label.

props.name: maxFontSizeMultiplier
props.description:
Specifies largest possible scale a font can reach when allowFontScaling is enabled. Possible values:
- null/undefined (default): inherit from the parent node or the global default (0)
- 0: no max, ignore parent/global default
- >= 1: sets the maxFontSizeMultiplier of this node to this value

props.name: hitSlop
props.description:
This defines how far a touch event can start away from the view.
Typical interface guidelines recommend touch targets that are at least
30 - 40 points/density-independent pixels. If a Touchable view has
a height of 20 the touchable height can be extended to 40 with
hitSlop={{top: 10, bottom: 10, left: 0, right: 0}}
NOTE The touch area never extends past the parent view bounds and
the Z-index of sibling views always takes precedence if a touch
hits two overlapping views.

props.name: id
props.description: Used to reference react managed views from native code.

props.name: needsOffscreenAlphaCompositing
props.description:
Whether this view needs to rendered offscreen and composited with an alpha in order to preserve 100% correct colors and blending behavior.
The default (false) falls back to drawing the component and its children
with an alpha applied to the paint used to draw each element instead of rendering the full component offscreen and compositing it back with an alpha value.
This default may be noticeable and undesired in the case where the View you are setting an opacity on
has multiple overlapping elements (e.g. multiple overlapping Views, or text and a background).

Rendering offscreen to preserve correct alpha behavior is extremely expensive
and hard to debug for non-native developers, which is why it is not turned on by default.
If you do need to enable this property for an animation,
consider combining it with renderToHardwareTextureAndroid if the view contents are static (i.e. it doesn't need to be redrawn each frame).
If that property is enabled, this View will be rendered off-screen once,
saved in a hardware texture, and then composited onto the screen with an alpha each frame without having to switch rendering targets on the GPU.

props.name: onLayout
props.description:
Invoked on mount and layout changes with

{nativeEvent: { layout: {x, y, width, height}}}.

props.name: pointerEvents
removeClippedSubviews
props.description:
This is a special performance property exposed by RCTView and is useful for scrolling content when there are many subviews,
most of which are offscreen. For this property to be effective, it must be applied to a view that contains many subviews that extend outside its bound.
The subviews must also have overflow: hidden, as should the containing view (or one of its superviews).

props.name: nativeID
props.description: Used to reference react managed views from native code.

props.name: collapsable
props.description:
Views that are only used to layout their children or otherwise don't draw anything
may be automatically removed from the native hierarchy as an optimization.
Set this property to false to disable this optimization and ensure that this View exists in the native view hierarchy.

props.name: collapsableChildren
props.description:
Setting to false prevents direct children of the view from being removed
from the native view hierarchy, similar to the effect of setting
`collapsable={false}` on each child.

props.name: renderToHardwareTextureAndroid
props.description:
Whether this view should render itself (and all of its children) into a single hardware texture on the GPU.

On Android, this is useful for animations and interactions that only modify opacity, rotation, translation, and/or scale:
in those cases, the view doesn't have to be redrawn and display lists don't need to be re-executed. The texture can just be
re-used and re-composited with different parameters. The downside is that this can use up limited video memory, so this prop should be set back to false at the end of the interaction/animation.

props.name: focusable
props.description: Whether this `View` should be focusable with a non-touch input device, eg. receive focus with a hardware keyboard.

props.name: tabIndex
props.description:
Indicates whether this `View` should be focusable with a non-touch input device, eg. receive focus with a hardware keyboard.
See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/tabindex
for more details.

Supports the following values:
-  0 (View is focusable)
- -1 (View is not focusable)

props.name: shouldRasterizeIOS
props.description:
Whether this view should be rendered as a bitmap before compositing.

On iOS, this is useful for animations and interactions that do not modify this component's dimensions nor its children;
for example, when translating the position of a static view, rasterization allows the renderer to reuse a cached bitmap of a static view
and quickly composite it during each frame.

Rasterization incurs an off-screen drawing pass and the bitmap consumes memory.
Test and measure when using this property.

props.name: isTVSelectable
props.description:
*(Apple TV only)* When set to true, this view will be focusable

props.name: hasTVPreferredFocus
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be set to true to force the Apple TV focus engine to move focus to this view.

props.name: tvParallaxShiftDistanceX
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus.  Defaults to 2.0.

props.name: tvParallaxShiftDistanceY
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus.  Defaults to 2.0.

props.name: tvParallaxTiltAngle
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus.  Defaults to 0.05.

props.name: tvParallaxMagnification
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus.  Defaults to 1.0.

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponder
props.description: Does this view want to become responder on the start of a touch?

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponder
props.description: Called for every touch move on the View when it is not the responder: does this view want to "claim" touch responsiveness?

props.name: onResponderEnd
props.description: If the View returns true and attempts to become the responder, one of the following will happen:

props.name: onResponderGrant
props.description:
The View is now responding for touch events.
This is the time to highlight and show the user what is happening

props.name: onResponderReject
props.description: Something else is the responder right now and will not release it

props.name: onResponderMove
props.description: The user is moving their finger

props.name: onResponderRelease
props.description: Fired at the end of the touch, ie "touchUp"

props.name: onResponderTerminationRequest
props.description:
Something else wants to become responder.
Should this view release the responder? Returning true allows release

props.name: onResponderTerminate
props.description:
The responder has been taken from the View.
Might be taken by other views after a call to onResponderTerminationRequest,
or might be taken by the OS without asking (happens with control center/ notification center on iOS)

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:
onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern,
where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.
This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable.

However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder.
This can be handled by using the capture phase.
Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component,
it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture.
So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:
onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern,
where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.
This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable.

However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder.
This can be handled by using the capture phase.
Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component,
it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture.
So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:
onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern,
where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.
This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable.

However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder.
This can be handled by using the capture phase.
Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component,
it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture.
So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.description:
onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern,
where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.
This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable.

However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder.
This can be handled by using the capture phase.
Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component,
it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture.
So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.
